_provenance.note: Do not hand-edit; regenerate from the neuroschema repo.

schemas.title: Dataset Metadata
schemas.description: Study-level metadata for a neuroimaging dataset. Contains what modalities are present, participant demographics (from participants.tsv), signal properties shared across recordings, event/HED annotation status, and provenance. Aligned with BIDS dataset_description.json and participants.tsv. Platform-neutral; platform-specific fields belong in extensions.

schema_version.description: Envelope field: schema version (present when validated through root schema).

doc_type.description: Envelope field: document type (present when validated through root schema).

dataset_id.description: Unique dataset identifier (e.g., 'ds003645' for OpenNeuro, 'nm000108' for NEMAR).

description.description: Short abstract or description of the dataset.

recording_modality.description: Recording modalities present in the dataset (e.g., ['EEG', 'MEG', 'MRI']). Dataset-level property; individual data files inherit their modality from the BIDS datatype directory.

bids_version.description: BIDS specification version the dataset follows.

authors.description: List of dataset authors as structured person objects.

funding.description: Funding sources with structured grant information.

funder_identifier.description: Persistent identifier for the funder (e.g., Crossref Funder ID, ROR ID).

award_uri.description: URI to the award or grant information page.

tasks.description: Experimental tasks present in the dataset.

datatypes.description: BIDS datatype directories present in the dataset (e.g., ['eeg', 'anat']).

sessions.description: Session labels present in the dataset (e.g., ['pre', 'post']).

sessions_count.description: Number of sessions in the dataset.

has_hed_annotations.description: Whether the dataset includes Hierarchical Event Descriptors (HED) annotations.

hed_version.description: Version of the HED schema used for annotations (e.g., '8.1.0').

has_event_annotations.description: Whether the dataset includes event/stimulus annotations (events.tsv files).

keywords.description: Subject terms and keywords for findability. Supports both plain keywords (term only) and controlled vocabulary entries (with scheme and URI). Aligns with DataCite Subject (property 6).

related_identifiers.description: Related resources: associated papers, source datasets, code repositories, prior versions. These links feed into scholarly knowledge graphs and citation indices. Aligns with DataCite RelatedIdentifier (property 12).

data_papers.description: Papers, or deposits of the same data, that a trusted judgment classified as this dataset's own data paper. More reliable than the relation type on related_identifiers, which is only a hint. Key absent means the dataset has not been judged yet; an empty array means it was judged and has no data paper. The dataset's own DOI is not listed here (see external_links).

contributors.description: Contributors with typed roles beyond the primary authors. Includes data collectors, hosting institutions, project leaders, etc. Aligns with DataCite Contributor (property 7).

dates.description: Semantically typed dates: data collection period, creation date, publication date, etc. Aligns with DataCite Date (property 8).

rights.description: Structured license/rights entries with URIs and machine-readable identifiers. Complements the simpler 'license' string field. Aligns with DataCite Rights (property 16).

language.description: Primary language of the dataset content (IETF BCP 47 tag, e.g., 'en'). Aligns with DataCite Language (property 9).

schemas.title: Person
schemas.description: A structured person record for authors or contributors. Includes name components, ORCID, and affiliations for DataCite compatibility.

name_type.description: Whether this is a person or organization. Defaults to Personal if omitted.

schemas.title: Demographics
schemas.description: Subject demographics summary at the dataset level.

subjects_count.description: Total number of subjects in the dataset.

schemas.title: Data Summary
schemas.description: Aggregate statistics about the data content of a dataset. These are computed summaries across all recordings (ranges, counts, distributions).

total_files.description: Total number of files in the dataset.

recording_count.description: Total number of recordings (data files) in the dataset.

recordings_unavailable.description: Number of recordings in the dataset that could not be summarised (truncated, corrupt, in an unsupported format, or otherwise unreadable). recording_count counts all recordings in the dataset, so recording_count minus recordings_unavailable gives the number of recordings with usable summaries.

total_recording_duration.description: Total recording duration in seconds, summed across recordings. Concurrent channel groups within a single recording are not additive: a recording with EEG and EOG streams running simultaneously contributes its longest stream to the sum, not the sum of both streams. The sum covers only recordings that could be summarised, so when recordings_unavailable is non-zero this value is a lower bound on the dataset's true total.

channel_count_range.description: Range of channel counts across recordings in this dataset.

channel_type_summary.description: Summary counts of channel types across the dataset (e.g., {'EEG': 64, 'EOG': 2, 'ECG': 1}).

sampling_frequency_range.description: Range of sampling frequencies across recordings (if they vary).

recording_duration_range.description: Range of per-recording durations across the dataset, in seconds.

data_processed.description: Whether the dataset contains processed (vs. raw) data.

schemas.title: Inheritable Signal Properties
schemas.description: Signal properties that follow the BIDS inheritance pattern: the dataset provides defaults and individual records can override them. Used in both dataset.signal_defaults and record.signal_properties.

power_line_frequency.description: Power line frequency in Hz (typically 50 or 60).

placement_scheme.description: Detailed electrode placement scheme from BIDS EEG sidecar (e.g., 'extended 10-10% system').

schemas.title: Provenance
schemas.description: Timestamps and origin tracking for the metadata document.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when the dataset was first created/published.

ingested_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when this metadata was ingested into the system.

latest_snapshot.description: Latest version/snapshot identifier of the dataset (e.g., '2.0.2').

uploader.description: Name of the person who uploaded the dataset.

schemas.title: Subject/Keyword
schemas.description: A structured subject term with optional controlled vocabulary linkage. Aligns with DataCite Subject (property 6). Supports free-text keywords and terms from controlled vocabularies like MeSH, Cognitive Atlas, or Library of Congress Subject Headings.

term.description: The subject term or keyword text.

subject_scheme.description: Name of the controlled vocabulary or classification scheme (e.g., 'MeSH', 'Cognitive Atlas', 'LCSH', 'Fields of Science and Technology (FOS)').

value_uri.description: URI identifying this specific subject term within the scheme.

classification_code.description: Classification code within the scheme (e.g., MeSH tree number, ANZSRC code). Use when the scheme does not provide per-term URIs.

schemas.title: Related Identifier
schemas.description: A link to a related resource with typed relationship. Aligns with DataCite RelatedIdentifier (property 12). Supports DOIs, URLs, PMIDs, arXiv IDs, and other persistent identifier types. These links feed into citation graphs and scholarly knowledge graphs.

identifier.description: The identifier value (e.g., '10.1234/example' for DOI, 'https://example.com' for URL).

identifier_type.description: Type of the identifier. Inferred from format if omitted.

relation_type.description: Relationship of the identified resource to this dataset. Framed as: this dataset [relation_type] the related resource.

resource_type_general.description: General type of the related resource (not this dataset). Enables graph-based filtering by resource type.

related_metadata_scheme.description: Name of the metadata scheme. Only applicable when relation_type is HasMetadata or IsMetadataFor.

schemas.title: Data Paper
schemas.description: A paper, or a deposit of the same data, that a trusted judgment classified as this dataset's own data paper: it introduces, describes, or releases the data in this specific dataset. Unlike the relation type on a related identifier, which is only a hint, membership here is a judged verdict.

doi.description: DOI of the data paper, without a resolver prefix (e.g., '10.1038/s41597-019-0027-4'): 10., four to nine ASCII digits, a slash, and a suffix of printable ASCII with no space. The classes are explicit, so Python and JavaScript read the pattern alike (\d and \S differ between them). DOIs are case-insensitive; the producer serves them in canonical lowercase, so consumers must compare case-insensitively (for example against related_identifiers[].identifier).

title.description: Title of the paper as resolved from the DOI registry. Null when it could not be resolved.

venue.description: Journal, preprint server, or repository that published it (e.g., 'Scientific Data', 'bioRxiv'). Null when unknown.

judge_model.description: Identifier of the model that made the data-paper judgment (e.g., 'claude-sonnet-5-5'), as recorded by the pipeline in its judgment_model field. Null when not recorded.

schemas.title: Contributor
schemas.description: A contributor with a typed role, beyond the primary authors/creators. Aligns with DataCite Contributor (property 7). Common roles for neuroimaging datasets include DataCollector, ProjectLeader, and HostingInstitution.

name.description: Full display name (e.g., 'Jane A. Smith' or 'NEMAR').

given_name.description: Given (first) name. Omit for organizational contributors.

family_name.description: Family (last) name. Omit for organizational contributors.

name_type.description: Whether this is a person or organization.

schemas.title: Structured Date
schemas.description: A date with semantic type. Aligns with DataCite Date (property 8). Supports single dates, date ranges (YYYY-MM-DD/YYYY-MM-DD), and year-only precision. Use 'Collected' for data acquisition periods, 'Issued' for publication date, 'Created' for dataset creation.

date_information.description: Free-text detail about the date (e.g., 'EEG recording sessions' for a Collected date).

schemas.title: Rights
schemas.description: A structured rights/license entry with URI and machine-readable identifier. Aligns with DataCite Rights (property 16). Complements the simpler 'license' string field in core by providing full SPDX identifiers and URIs needed for DOI registration and FAIR compliance.

rights.description: Human-readable rights statement (e.g., 'Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International').

schemas.title: External Links
schemas.description: Relevant external hyperlinks for the dataset.

source_url.description: URL to the primary data source (e.g., OpenNeuro page).

references_and_links.description: List of references and publication links.

dataset_doi.description: Digital Object Identifier for the dataset.

associated_paper_doi.description: DOI of the primary associated paper.

osf_url.description: URL to the Open Science Framework (OSF) project.

github_url.description: URL to the associated GitHub repository.

paper_url.description: URL to the primary associated paper (if not a DOI).

schemas.title: Extensions Container
schemas.description: Container for domain-specific extensions using reserved namespaces. Each project or domain gets its own namespace. Adding new top-level namespaces requires a MINOR schema version bump. Follows the pattern established by signalJourney's extension system.

signalJourney.description: Namespace for links to the signalJourney records of NEMAR recipe runs, one per recipe.

nemar.description: Namespace for NEMAR-specific properties (API fields, legacy fields).

dataQuality.description: Namespace for quality results (metrics and views) projected from the signalJourney records of NEMAR recipe runs, per recording and per dataset.

processing.description: Namespace for checkpoint outcomes of NEMAR recipe runs (per recording and per dataset).

rawDetail.description: Namespace for detailed per-channel arrays (channel names, types, TSV data). Separated from core to keep core documents lean.

dataCite.description: Namespace for DataCite DOI registration metadata (publisher, resource type, geo_locations, alternate_identifiers, related_items). Note: keywords, related_identifiers, contributors, dates, rights, and language moved to core in v0.3.0.

dataCategories.description: Namespace for study classification (paradigm, clinical context, cognitive domains).

x-extension-managers.description: Maps each extension namespace to its owning service and MongoDB collection. Core fields are platform-neutral; extension collections have separate access control per service.

schemas.title: EEGDash Extension
schemas.description: EEGDash-specific metadata for visualization and streaming. Fields that support the EEGDash dashboard but are not part of the core neuroschema.

storage.description: Storage location details for EEGDash backend.

base.description: Base URI for the storage location.

raw_key.description: Relative path key to the raw file.

senior_author.description: Senior/corresponding author name for display purposes.

contact_info.description: Contact information for the dataset (email or URL).

ages.description: Raw array of participant ages. Core has summary statistics only (age_min, age_max, age_mean); this holds the full distribution.

schemas.title: signalJourney Extension
schemas.description: Links from a dataset or recording to the signalJourney records of NEMAR recipe runs, one per recipe, written by the NEMAR backend. The same shape at both levels. A link describes the latest run: `in_progress` while reports arrive (no record yet), `completed` when the run wrote this record, `failed` when the run ended without writing it (the reason is in the processing extension). dataQuality keeps the last completed results.

recipes.description: Record link per recipe, keyed by recipe id.

recordLink.description: Link to one recipe run's signalJourney record. location, sha256 and sj_version are set when completed and null otherwise: null while in_progress (no record yet) and null when failed (the run ended without writing this record).

recipe_version.description: Version of the recipe whose run this link describes.

processing_status.description: State of the latest run of this recipe.

location.description: Path of the signalJourney record inside the run's product.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the signalJourney record's bytes.

sj_version.description: Version of the signalJourney specification the record follows.

schemas.title: Processing Types
schemas.description: Shared types for the dataQuality, processing and signalJourney extensions and the view declaration. A library of $defs; the root constrains nothing.

recipeId.description: Identifier of a NEMAR processing recipe (for example nemar-floor), lowercase letters, digits and hyphens.

version.description: A version label (recipe, dataset or plugin version) of letters, digits and . _ + -.

sha256.description: Lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest of a file's bytes.

checkpointName.description: Name of a processing checkpoint: a coarse stage a recipe declares. Open vocabulary; the writer checks it against the checkpoints the recipe version declares.

stepId.description: Identifier of a recipe step (the step names of a recipe's step order).

failureCode.description: Machine-readable failure or skip code, lowercase snake case.

metricName.description: Name of a quality metric, safe as a document key (no . or $): a recipe's metric by a bare name, or a plugin's by <plugin>:<name>, one colon and a name after it that starts with a letter. The prefix has the plugin name's grammar (plugin.name), so every plugin can name its metrics. In a recording's dataQuality metrics each name is paired with its producer (dataQuality.schema.json, recordRecipeResults.metrics: a bare name requires recipe, a prefixed one plugin); that the prefix is the producing plugin's name is the writer's rule.

relativeLocation.description: Relative POSIX path inside a run's product, as Unicode text written in UTF-8, and never a URL: no leading slash, no URI scheme, no . or .. segment, no empty segment (no // and no trailing /), no backslash, none of % ? # (so nothing in it decodes or resolves into something else), no leading or trailing space, no control character (C0 U+0000 to U+001F, DEL U+007F, C1 U+0080 to U+009F), no line or paragraph separator (U+2028, U+2029: a JavaScript . does not match them, so a lookahead would stop there) and no bidirectional control (U+061C, U+200E, U+200F, U+202A to U+202E, U+2066 to U+2069). A renderer that fetches it percent-encodes the UTF-8 bytes of each segment and joins the segments with / (docs/views.md, Data roles).

inputKind.description: What a run read: a BIDS dataset directory or NEMAR's Zarr serving copy.

profile.description: Which copy of the data a run's results describe: the archived recordings or the serving copy.

inputProfilePairing.description: A zarr input always describes the serving copy and a bids input the archive.

range.description: A closed numeric range; either end may be null when unbounded or unknown.

plugin.description: The quality plugin, by name and version, that produced a value or view.

name.description: Plugin name as declared in its manifest: a letter, then letters, digits, _ and -, at most 64 characters. The grammar of a metricName prefix, so <plugin>:<name> can name every plugin's metric and stays a safe document key (no . or $).

version.description: Plugin version as declared in its manifest.

recipe.description: The NEMAR processing recipe, by id and version, that produced a value or view.

viewKey.description: Key of a view declaration, unique within its recipe entry: lowercase letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter.

kindName.description: Namespaced name of a view kind (for example nemar.table): a lowercase namespace, then one or more dot-separated segments of lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. Open vocabulary; views/registry.json lists the kinds neuroschema defines.

transformName.description: Namespaced, versioned name of a view transform (for example nemar.ic-activity.v1): a name shaped like a kind name, then .v and the version number (1 to 999).

roleName.description: Name of a data role or input role in a view (for example values, layout): lowercase letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter.

dimName.description: Name of a dimension of a view's data (for example sensor, freq). Open vocabulary; views/registry.json lists the reserved names and their fixed meanings.

formatName.description: Name of a view data format (tsv or json today). Open vocabulary; views/registry.json lists the formats and their grammars.

schemas.title: NEMAR Extension
schemas.description: NEMAR-specific properties that extend the core schema. Includes fields from the NEMAR API and nemar.json that are not part of the universal core.

on_brainlife.description: Whether the dataset is available on BrainLife.

has_visualization.description: Whether NEMAR has generated visualizations for this dataset.

nemar_json.description: Contents of the nemar.json file (warnings, plots, channel system info).

local_dataset.description: Whether a local copy of the dataset is maintained by NEMAR.

processed.description: Whether NEMAR has processed this dataset.

hed_annotation.description: Whether the dataset has HED annotations (from NEMAR processing).

citation_count.description: Number of papers citing this dataset (from NEMAR citations repository).

schemas.title: Data Quality Extension
schemas.description: Quality results the NEMAR backend projects from the signalJourney records of its recipe runs. `level` selects the shape: `record` (one recording's metrics and views per recipe) or `dataset` (the dataset quality control summary per recipe; replaces nemar-process qc-summary.v1). Each entry carries the SHA-256 of the signalJourney record it came from; the record stays the source. Closed at every level, its root and its $defs included: it holds the views a browser draws, so a member no schema checks (a second views list, a stray counts block) is refused rather than carried along.

level.description: Which document this entry belongs to: record (one recording) or dataset (the whole dataset).

recipes.description: Results per recipe, keyed by recipe id; the level's shape ($defs/record or $defs/dataset) constrains each entry.
Results per recipe, keyed by recipe id.
Quality control summary per recipe, keyed by recipe id.

recordRecipeResults.description: One recording's quality results from one recipe run.

recipe_version.description: Version of the recipe that produced these results.

profile.description: Which copy of the data the results describe.

record_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the bytes of the recording's signalJourney record these values were projected from.

metrics.description: Metrics keyed by metric name (processingTypes metricName): a recipe's own metric by a bare name, with the producer recipe, and a plugin's by <plugin>:<name>, with the producer plugin. That the prefix is the producing plugin's name is the writer's rule.

^[^:]+$(?!\n).description: A recipe's metric, by a bare name.

views.description: Quality views for this recording: data a browser draws, with their declarations (definitions/view.schema.json). Keys are unique within the entry.

views_skipped.description: The views the run declares for a recording and did not write for this one, each with the reason, so a renderer says why a view is absent rather than leaving it out silently (docs/views.md, Views a run skipped). Optional; keys are unique, and none is the key of a view in views (the writer's rule).

then.description: Every store input of the entry's views names the copy the entry's run read: the store's profile is the entry's.
Every store input of the entry's views names the copy the entry's run read: the store's profile is the entry's.

viewSkipped.description: A view the run did not write for this recording: its key and kind, as the run would have declared them, and why.

key.description: The view's key, as the run declares it for other recordings.

reason.description: Why the view was not written: a word of docs/views.md (labels_unusable, plugin_failed, step_failed, step_skipped, cap_exceeded), or another word, which a renderer shows as it is.

datasetRecipeSummary.description: The dataset quality control summary from one recipe run.

recipe_version.description: Version of the recipe that produced this summary.

dataset_version.description: Dataset version the run processed; null when unversioned.

profile.description: Which copy of the data the summary describes.

record_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the bytes of the dataset-level signalJourney record this summary was derived from.

counts.description: Recordings passed, failed, skipped and discovered by the run.

distributions.description: Distribution of each metric over the recordings that passed, keyed by metric name. Bins are [e_i, e_i+1), the last bin closed.

observed_range.description: Lowest and highest value of each metric observed across the recordings that passed (for example good channels, good data, brain components), keyed by metric name. Not a metric's bounds, which is the valid range its plugin declares.

not_processed.description: Recordings that failed or were skipped, at most 200.

not_processed_truncated.description: Number of not-processed recordings left out of not_processed by its cap.

distribution.description: Summary of one metric's values over the recordings that passed.

unit.description: Unit of the metric's values (for example %, dB, count), as its producer states it.

description.description: One-sentence description of what the metric measures, as its producer states it.

min.description: Smallest value; null when n is 0.

median.description: Median value; null when n is 0.

max.description: Largest value; null when n is 0.

counts.description: Count per bin; one fewer than the edges.

missing.description: Recordings whose value was missing or not a number, so in no bin and not in n, counted apart.

notProcessed.description: A recording the run did not process to the end.

status.description: Whether the recording failed or was skipped.

code.description: The recording's first failure or skip code.

schemas.title: Quality Metric
schemas.description: One quality metric computed for a recording, with exactly one producer. A plugin manifest (nemar-cli shared/contract) declares each of its metric outputs with this shape and names the producer with plugin; recipe is for a metric a recipe writes into its own records.

value.description: The metric's value; null when it could not be computed.

unit.description: Unit of the value (for example %, dB, count).

description.description: One-sentence description of what the metric measures.

bounds.description: The valid range the producer declares for this value (for example 0 to 100 for a percentage), not a quality threshold and not the range observed across recordings (that is the dataset summary's observed_range).

plugin.description: The plugin that produced this value; the producer of every metric a plugin manifest declares. Exactly one of plugin and recipe.

recipe.description: The recipe that produced this value, for a metric a recipe writes into its own records. Exactly one of plugin and recipe.

schemas.title: View Declaration
schemas.description: A quality view: data that a browser draws, declared by the recipe or plugin that wrote it. A library of $defs; the root constrains nothing, and $defs/view is the declaration. Every view is checked against this envelope. A kind and version that views/registry.json lists is also checked against its schema in schema/views/, and so is a transform it lists; any other kind or transform passes on the envelope alone, and a renderer draws it by its base or as a table (docs/views.md).

key.description: The view's key, unique within its recipe entry.

kind.description: The view's kind. Open: a kind this schema does not know is valid.

kind_version.description: Version of the kind; a change to a kind is a new version.

base.description: The generic kind a preset draws over. Required for a preset, absent for a generic kind (each kind's schema says which); always given with base_version. Never one of the presets views/registry.json lists: a preset is drawn over a generic kind and is no base itself.

base_version.description: Version of the base kind; always given with base.

scope.description: What the view describes; absent means recording. subject, dataset and collection are reserved: they require sources, and nothing writes or reads them yet.

sources.description: The records a view of a reserved scope summarizes. Required for a scope other than recording and absent for a recording view.

parameters.description: How the data were computed or are to be drawn. Open here; each kind's schema constrains it.

data.description: Stored data files, one per role.

inputs.description: Inputs a transform computes the view from, named by digest.

transform.description: The named, versioned computation over the inputs; required exactly when the kind's schema requires it.

sources.description: A recording view has no sources.

viewSource.description: What wrote a view: exactly one of a plugin or a recipe, by name and version.

plugin.description: The plugin that wrote the view.

recipe.description: The recipe that wrote the view.

scopeSource.description: One record a view of a reserved scope summarizes.

record_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the bytes of the signalJourney record.

viewData.description: One stored data file of a view, read as one role. A role reads only the columns it declares, so one file can serve two roles.

role.description: The role this file plays in the view's kind.

location.description: Path of the file inside the run's product; the same string as its signalJourney outputTargets location.

format.description: The file's format; views/registry.json gives its grammar. A tsv or json file's location ends in .tsv or .json, and a location that ends in .tsv or .json, in any case, is a file of that format. A renderer offers a file of a format the registry does not list for download only, as an attachment of type application/octet-stream (docs/views.md, Formats).

size.description: Size of the file in bytes; at most views/registry.json caps.bytes_per_role (4,194,304), which a renderer checks before it fetches the file.

columns.description: The columns this role reads, by header name.

dims.description: The dimensions of this role's data and where their coordinates come from.

coordinate_system.description: For a role of sensor positions: the BIDS name of the coordinate system, or n/a.

position_source.description: For a role of sensor positions: measured (taken from the dataset's own files, which NEMAR does not verify) or template (a standard montage matched by label).

montage.description: For a role of template sensor positions: the montage they were taken from, by its name in views/montages (nemar.sensor-labels.v1, docs/views/sensor-labels.md). Given exactly with position_source template, with coordinate_system n/a; the positions are read as RAS meters, the montage's frame.

cap_model.description: For a role whose sensors a renderer may place by name (nemar.sensor-labels.v1, docs/views/sensor-labels.md): the recording's BIDS CapManufacturersModelName, as its eeg.json gives it after BIDS inheritance. A placement on an EGI HydroCel net needs it to name the net.

reference.description: For a role whose sensors a renderer may place by name (nemar.sensor-labels.v1): the recording's BIDS EEGReference, as its eeg.json gives it after BIDS inheritance. The placed channel it names is the reference channel, which a scalp map leaves out only when all its values are exactly zero (docs/views/sensor-field.md).

format.description: A file named .tsv, in any case, is a tsv file: the extension names the format in both directions.
A file named .json, in any case, is a json file.

columnName.description: A header name in a tabular file: no TAB, CR or LF.

valueType.description: Type of a cell or coordinate: number (finite, JSON number grammar), integer, or string.

dim.description: One dimension of a role's data. Reserved names (views/registry.json) have fixed meanings; time is in seconds.

axis.description: Whether the dimension runs along the file's rows or its columns.

coords.description: Where a dimension's coordinates come from: a column of this file ({column}), this file's header names ({header: true}), or, by position, a column of another role ({role, column}).

viewInput.description: One input of a computed view: exactly one of a derivative file or a serving store, each named by its digest.

role.description: The role this input plays in the view's transform.

file.description: A file of the run's product.

store.description: A recording's store in NEMAR's serving copy.

fileInput.description: A file of the run's product, named by its digest.

location.description: Path of the file inside the run's product; the same string as its signalJourney outputTargets location.

size.description: Size of the file in bytes; at most views/registry.json caps.bytes_per_role (4,194,304), which a renderer checks before it fetches the file.

storeInput.description: A recording's store in NEMAR's serving copy, named by its nemar.store-content.v1 digest.

path.description: The store's path, as in the record's stores_content rows, when it is not the recording path.

group.description: The channel group the transform reads (for example eeg).

content_sha256.description: The group's nemar.store-content.v1 digest; null only when the run read the archive (profile archive), which records no digest of the serving store.

profile.description: Which copy of the data the run that declared the view read.

transform.description: A named, versioned computation over a view's inputs, with its parameters.

parameters.description: The transform's parameters; the transform's schema constrains them.

schemas.title: View Kind nemar.table, Version 1
schemas.description: A generic table, applied to a view declaration whose kind is nemar.table and kind_version 1, on top of the envelope. One stored TSV file read as the role table; a renderer shows the declared columns in the order declared, one row per data row, each cell as its stored text, and offers the file for download. A generic kind: no base, no inputs, no transform, no parameters and no dimensions.

base.description: A generic kind has no base.

base_version.description: A generic kind has no base.

inputs.description: A table is stored data only.

transform.description: A table is stored data only.

dims.description: A table role carries no dimensions.

data.description: Exactly one file, read as the role table.

schemas.title: View Kind nemar.lines, Version 1
schemas.description: Generic line chart, applied on top of the envelope to a view declaration whose kind is nemar.lines and kind_version 1. One stored TSV file is read as the role values. One dimension runs along the rows: its coordinates are a numeric column of the file, strictly increasing, and they form the x axis. The other runs along the columns: each declared column other than the x column is one series. The series labels are the column names, or, for a preset over this kind, a column of another of the preset's roles. A renderer builds the model in docs/views/generic-kinds.md. This is a generic kind, so it has no base, no inputs, no transform and no parameters.

base.description: A generic kind has no base.

base_version.description: A generic kind has no base.

inputs.description: A line chart is stored data only.

transform.description: A line chart is stored data only.

data.description: Exactly one file, read as the role values.

items.description: The role values: the x column and one numeric column per series. A preset drawn over this kind meets this subschema with its own values entry (docs/views.md, the role contract).

columns.description: The x column and the series columns, all numeric. The series are the declared columns other than the x column, in declared order.

dims.description: Exactly two dimensions with open names: the x dimension along the rows, with its coordinates in a numeric column of this file, and the series dimension along the columns, with its coordinates in the header or in another role.

allOf.description: A view of this kind has only the role values, so none of its coordinates comes from another role. The rule sits at the root, outside data, so a preset drawn by this kind leaves it out of the role contract it meets, and may take coordinates from one of its own roles.

schemas.title: View Kind nemar.heatmap, Version 1
schemas.description: Generic heatmap, applied on top of the envelope to a view declaration whose kind is nemar.heatmap and kind_version 1. One stored TSV file is read as the role values: a matrix of numeric cells, drawn one flat cell per stored value with no interpolation. One dimension runs along the rows: its labels are a column of the file, or, for a preset over this kind, a column of another of the preset's roles. The other runs along the columns: each declared column other than the row-label column is one column of the matrix, and its label is the column name or comes from another role. A renderer builds the model in docs/views/generic-kinds.md. This is a generic kind, so it has no base, no inputs and no transform.

base.description: A generic kind has no base.

base_version.description: A generic kind has no base.

inputs.description: A heatmap is stored data only.

transform.description: A heatmap is stored data only.

limits.description: minmax spans the smallest to the largest cell with a sequential map; absmax spans minus to plus the largest absolute cell with a diverging map centered on zero.

data.description: Exactly one file, read as the role values.

items.description: The role values: an optional row-label column and one numeric column per matrix column. A preset drawn over this kind meets this subschema with its own values entry (docs/views.md, the role contract).

columns.description: The row-label column, when the row labels are in this file, and the matrix columns, in declared order. Matrix columns are numeric; the model refuses a text one (value_type).

dims.description: Exactly two dimensions with open names: the row dimension, with its labels in a column of this file or of another role, and the column dimension, with its labels in the header or in another role.

allOf.description: A view of this kind has only the role values, so none of its coordinates comes from another role. The rule sits at the root, outside data, so a preset drawn by this kind leaves it out of the role contract it meets, and may take coordinates from one of its own roles.

schemas.title: View Kind nemar.histogram, Version 1
schemas.description: Generic histogram, applied on top of the envelope to a view declaration whose kind is nemar.histogram and kind_version 1. One stored JSON file is read as the role histogram, and its content meets content.nemar.histogram.v1. The content holds counts per bin, binned either by numeric edges or by named categories, and a renderer draws the stated counts without recomputing them. A renderer builds the model in docs/views/generic-kinds.md. This is a generic kind, so it has no base, no inputs, no transform, no parameters and no dimensions.

base.description: A generic kind has no base.

base_version.description: A generic kind has no base.

inputs.description: A histogram is stored data only.

transform.description: A histogram is stored data only.

data.description: Exactly one file, read as the role histogram.

items.description: The role histogram: one JSON file whose content meets content.nemar.histogram.v1. A preset drawn over this kind meets this subschema with its own histogram entry (docs/views.md, the role contract).

columns.description: A JSON role has no columns.

dims.description: The bins are in the content, not in dimensions.

content.description: The schema the role's file meets. It is not applied to the declaration; this reference names it, so a tool that bundles the schemas a declaration reaches also bundles the content schema.

schemas.title: Histogram Content, Version 1
schemas.description: The content of the role histogram of a nemar.histogram view: counts per bin, with the bins given either as numeric edges, where bin i holds e_i <= v < e_(i+1) and the last bin also holds v equal to the last edge, or as named categories. Its shape is the shape of a dataQuality distribution's histogram, with an optional unit; either form may count the values that were missing or not a number (missing). The root is open: a preset over nemar.histogram may add members of its own, and a renderer that draws the preset by this base reads only the members below. docs/views/generic-kinds.md gives the model and the rules JSON Schema cannot state: edges strictly increasing, and one count per bin.

edges.description: Bin edges, strictly increasing; one more than the counts. At most 1,024 bins (views/registry.json caps.entries_per_dim).

categories.description: Bin names, in drawing order, with no TAB, CR or LF; as many as the counts.

counts.description: Count per bin, in bin order, at most 2^53 - 1 so that every JSON parser reads it exactly.

unit.description: Unit of the binned values; edge bins only.

missing.description: Values that were missing or not a number, so in no bin, counted apart (in either form); a renderer shows the count beside the bars, never as one.

oneOf.description: Bins by category: no edges, no underflow or overflow, and no unit.

schemas.title: View Kind nemar.sensor-field, Version 1
schemas.description: A generic scalp map, applied on top of the envelope to a view declaration whose kind is nemar.sensor-field and kind_version 1. The role values holds one or more maps, each one value per sensor. The sensors are placed by one of three sources: the role layout (each sensor's theta and radius), the role positions (each sensor's x, y and z, which the transform nemar.sensor-layout.v1 projects to a layout, and which the view then declares as its transform), or, with neither, the sensor names, which a renderer places by nemar.sensor-labels.v1. A view has at most one of layout and positions, and the values' sensor coordinates are that role's name column, by position. The role that names the sensors (positions, or values with no sensor role) may carry the recording's cap_model and reference, which a placement by name reads; a layout carries neither. A renderer draws each map with the algorithm nemar.sensor-field.v1 (docs/views/sensor-field.md). A generic kind: no base and no inputs.

base.description: A generic kind has no base.

base_version.description: A generic kind has no base.

inputs.description: A scalp map is drawn from stored data only.

transform.description: With the role positions, the transform nemar.sensor-layout.v1, which projects them; without it, none.

limits.description: The color limits: absmax is symmetric about zero (plus and minus the largest magnitude, for a diverging map); minmax is the smallest and largest value (for a sequential map). Absent means absmax.

data.description: The role values, exactly once; at most one of the roles layout and positions.

oneOf.description: The role values: one or more maps over the sensor dimension. With the sensor dimension along the rows, each declared number column is a map; along the columns, each data row is a map, and the declared number columns are the sensors. A second dimension, of any name, along the other axis labels the maps.

dims.description: The sensor dimension, and at most one more along the other axis.

anyOf.description: Sensors along the rows: names in a column of this file, or the layout's rows.
Sensors along the columns: names in this file's header, or the layout's rows.

then.description: Two dimensions run along different axes.

oneOf.description: The role layout: each sensor's name, theta in degrees and radius (EEGLAB's topoplot coordinates: theta 0 at the nose and 90 at the right ear, radius 0.5 at the head's equator), one row per sensor, with the frame the layout came from and whether its positions were measured or taken from a template.

columns.description: name, theta_deg and radius, each once, and sensor_type, required when position_source is measured.

dims.description: The sensor dimension along the rows, named by the name column.

cap_model.description: A layout is drawn as stored and never placed by name, so it carries no cap model.

reference.description: A layout is drawn as stored and never placed by name, so it carries no reference.

allOf.description: A measured layout carries sensor_type: a scalp map draws the rows typed EEG and no untyped row, so an intracranial set that does not say what it is never reaches a scalp (the renderer refuses rows none of which is typed EEG with no_eeg_sensors). Template positions, from a montage, may be untyped.

oneOf.description: The role positions: each sensor's name and three-dimensional position (x, y and z, in one unit), one row per sensor, in the frame coordinate_system names, or, for template positions, with the coordinate system n/a and the montage they came from (the envelope's rule for a template role). The view's transform nemar.sensor-layout.v1 projects them to a layout.

columns.description: name, x, y and z, each once, and sensor_type, required when position_source is measured.

dims.description: The sensor dimension along the rows, named by the name column.

allOf.description: Measured positions carry sensor_type: a scalp map draws the rows typed EEG and no untyped row, so an intracranial set that does not say what it is never reaches a scalp (the renderer refuses rows none of which is typed EEG with no_eeg_sensors). Template positions, from a montage, may be untyped.
At most one of layout and positions places the sensors.

then.description: With a layout, the values' sensors are its rows: coordinates {role: layout, column: name}.
With positions, the values' sensors are its rows: coordinates {role: positions, column: name}.
With neither, the values' sensors are named in the values file.
Positions are projected by the declared transform.

transform.description: Without positions, a scalp map has no transform.

schemas.title: View Kind nemar.spectrum, Version 1
schemas.description: A power spectrum per sensor, a preset over nemar.lines version 1, applied on top of the envelope to a view declaration whose kind is nemar.spectrum and kind_version 1. The role values is a nemar.lines values entry: the column freq_hz (the dimension freq, in Hz) along the rows and one column per sensor (the dimension sensor, in dB) along the columns. The optional role layout places the sensors, so a renderer that knows this kind also draws a scalp map of the sensors' values at a chosen frequency row (nemar.sensor-field.v1); with a layout the sensors are its rows, by position, and without one they are the values' header names. The parameters record how the spectrum was computed. docs/views/presets.md is normative; a renderer that knows only nemar.lines draws the values entry as lines, because each entry meets its base's role subschema.

inputs.description: A spectrum is stored data only.

transform.description: A spectrum is stored data only.

parameters.description: How the spectrum was computed, recorded for the reader; a renderer prints them and recomputes nothing.

method.description: Welch's method: the mean of the periodograms of overlapping windows of window_s seconds, each detrended by its own mean and tapered by window; one-sided (the power above 0 and below half the rate doubled); the 0 Hz row left out by rule, since detrending each window by its mean makes it meaningless (docs/views/presets.md).

window.description: The taper applied to each window, by its lowercase name (hamming for NEMAR's spectra).

window_s.description: The length of each window, in seconds.

overlap.description: The share of each window that overlaps the next, from 0 up to but not including 1 (0.5 is half).

unit.description: Power spectral density in decibels relative to 1 microvolt squared per hertz: 10 log10 of the density in uV^2/Hz. The sensor columns carry the same unit.

upper_hz.description: The highest frequency the rows reach, in hertz: every freq_hz cell is at most this, and at most half the sampling rate.

initial_maps_hz.description: Frequencies whose scalp maps a renderer shows before the reader picks one, each drawn at the row nearest it by the nemar.lines readout rule.

data.description: The role values, exactly once, and the optional role layout.

oneOf.description: The role values: a nemar.lines values entry (it meets that role's subschema), with the column freq_hz in Hz as the x column and one column per sensor in dB.

columns.description: freq_hz once, in Hz, then the sensor columns, each a number in dB.

dims.description: The dimension freq along the rows and the dimension sensor along the columns.

contains.description: The frequency axis: the column freq_hz, in Hz.

oneOf.description: The role layout: each sensor's name, theta and radius, as nemar.sensor-field's role layout declares them (it meets that role's subschema).

then.description: With a layout, the sensors are its rows: coordinates {role: layout, column: name}.

else.description: Without a layout, the sensors are the values' header names.

sensorsFromLayout.description: The values' sensors are the layout's rows, by position.

sensorsFromHeader.description: The values' sensors are its header names.

schemas.title: View Kind nemar.ic-maps, Version 1
schemas.description: The scalp maps of the independent components of one decomposition, a preset over nemar.sensor-field version 1, applied on top of the envelope to a view declaration whose kind is nemar.ic-maps and kind_version 1. The role values is the mixing matrix, the sensors along the rows (the layout's rows, by position) and one map per component column (the dimension component, named by the header); the role layout places the sensors; the role components has one row per component, which a renderer prints as that component's text row. docs/views/presets.md is normative; a renderer that knows only nemar.sensor-field draws the values and the layout as maps, because they meet its role contract, and offers the components file for download.

inputs.description: Component maps are stored data only.

transform.description: The layout is stored, so no transform projects positions.

parameters.description: Version 1 takes no parameters: each map's color limits are absmax, symmetric about zero, because a component's polarity is arbitrary.

data.description: The roles values, layout and components, each exactly once.

oneOf.description: The role values: the mixing matrix, sensors by components. It meets nemar.sensor-field's role values; the sensors run along the rows and are the layout's rows, and each declared column is one component's map.

columns.description: One number column per component, in the decomposition's order.

dims.description: The sensors along the rows, from the layout, and the components along the columns, by header name.

oneOf.description: The role layout: each sensor's name, theta and radius, as nemar.sensor-field's role layout declares them.

The role components: one row per component, named in the column component, whose other declared columns (such as variance_pct and the class probabilities) a renderer prints as that component's text row.

columns.description: The column component, a string, once; the others in the order a text row prints them.

dims.description: The components along the rows, named by the column component.

allOf.description: The layout is required: the components were classified on these positions, and no map is drawn from names.

schemas.title: View Kind nemar.ic-classes, Version 1
schemas.description: The independent components of one decomposition counted by their dominant class, a preset over nemar.histogram version 1, applied on top of the envelope to a view declaration whose kind is nemar.ic-classes and kind_version 1. One stored JSON file is read as the role histogram; its content meets content.nemar.ic-classes.v1, a histogram by category (categories and counts) with the variance each class's components account for (summed_variance_pct) and the number of components (n_components). docs/views/presets.md is normative; a renderer that knows only nemar.histogram draws the categories and counts.

inputs.description: Class counts are stored data only.

transform.description: Class counts are stored data only.

data.description: Exactly one file, read as the role histogram.

items.description: The role histogram: one JSON file whose content meets content.nemar.ic-classes.v1. It meets nemar.histogram's role histogram.

columns.description: A JSON role has no columns.

dims.description: The classes are in the content, not in dimensions.

content.description: The schema the role's file meets. It is not applied to the declaration; this reference names it, so a tool that bundles the schemas a declaration reaches also bundles the content schema.

schemas.title: Component Classes Content, Version 1
schemas.description: The content of the role histogram of a nemar.ic-classes view: the independent components of one decomposition counted by the class each is most likely to be (its dominant class), with the variance the components of each class account for. It is a histogram content binned by category (content.nemar.histogram.v1), so a renderer that draws the view by its base nemar.histogram reads categories and counts; this preset adds the classifier (with ICLabel, the categories are exactly its seven classes in its order), summed_variance_pct and n_components. docs/views/presets.md gives the rules JSON Schema cannot state: one summed_variance_pct per category, and counts that sum to n_components.

categories.description: ICLabel's seven classes, in ICLabel's order and spelling.

classifier.description: ICLabel is spelled as ICLabel spells it, so its categories cannot be left open by a change of case or by I, l, 1 or | in place of one another (ICLabeI, lCLabel).

The classifier that gave each component's class probabilities, by name: printable ASCII only (U+0021 to U+007E, and the space inside), so no look-alike (a Cyrillic letter, a Roman numeral, a fullwidth form, a variation selector or a format character) can pass for a known name. ICLabel fixes the categories; any other name leaves them open.

items.description: A class name in printable ASCII, with no space at either end, so two names that look alike are two different texts.

categories.description: The classes, in the classifier's order (for ICLabel: Brain, Muscle, Eye, Heart, Line Noise, Channel Noise, Other), each in printable ASCII.

counts.description: For each class, the number of components whose most probable class it is; each component is counted once.

summed_variance_pct.description: For each class, in category order, the sum of the variance_pct of the components counted in it: the percent of the data's variance each component accounts for on its own (EEGLAB's pvaf), which is not bounded to 0 to 100 and does not sum to 100 across components.

n_components.description: The number of components of the decomposition; the counts sum to it.

schemas.title: View Kind nemar.ic-activity, Version 1
schemas.description: The activations of the independent components of one decomposition over a window of the recording, computed in the browser and never stored, a preset over nemar.lines version 1, applied on top of the envelope to a view declaration whose kind is nemar.ic-activity and kind_version 1. The transform nemar.ic-activity.v1 multiplies the serving copy's physical values of the decomposition's channels by the browser's unmixing matrix, with no preprocessing; its output is drawn as lines, time in seconds along x and one series per component. The parameters declare the display filter a renderer applies to what it draws (a zero-phase high-pass that is not part of the decomposition), the longest window it computes, and what the decomposition was given (decomposition_input), so the view can say how its activations differ from the decomposition's. docs/views/ic-activity.md is normative.

base.description: The transform's output is drawn as nemar.lines.

data.description: Activations are computed in the browser and never stored.

name.description: The transform's schema checks the inputs it reads and its parameters.

inputs.description: The roles unmixing, signal and components, each once (the transform's schema requires them), and badsegments exactly when the record names the floor's bad-segment table (shaded.files not null). No other role.

oneOf.description: A file of the run's product: the browser's unmixing matrix, the components table, or the bad segments a renderer shades.
The recording's store in the serving copy.

allOf.description: At most one badsegments input, declared exactly when the transform's shaded.files is not null (transform.nemar.ic-activity.v1's rule, which holds for every view that names the transform): the table is absent only when the floor's window step was skipped and ASR repaired nothing.

parameters.description: How the activations are drawn, and what the decomposition was given.

display_filter.description: The zero-phase high-pass a renderer applies to each component's activations before drawing them: over the window and up to a second of real context on each side, which it then discards, padded only at the recording's own ends (docs/views/ic-activity.md, the display filter). It is for display only and is not part of the decomposition.

highpass_hz.description: The cutoff, in hertz, where each pass is 3 dB down, so the two passes together are 6 dB down there and 3 dB down at about 1.246 times it; below half the store's sampling rate.

order.description: A Butterworth of order 2, run forward and backward.

max_window_s.description: The longest window, in seconds, a renderer computes at once.

decomposition_input.description: What the decomposition was given, as the run's record states it.

then.description: A decomposition of the archive declares a signal store of profile archive.
A decomposition of the serving copy declares a signal store of profile serving.

decompositionInput.description: What the decomposition was given, as nemar-process writes it in the record's extensions.nemar.ica.decomposition_input: where its input came from (source), the steps that shaped it in the order they ran (preprocessing), its channels, the type of every row of the loaded recording (channel_types) with their digest, its reference and its unit, and, for an input read from the serving copy, that store. The activations this view draws apply none of the preprocessing, so they approximate the decomposition's input.

source.description: archive: the dataset's own files (profile archive); serving_copy: NEMAR's Zarr serving copy (profile serving).

preprocessing.description: The steps that changed the data the decomposition received, in the order they ran, each by its step id and the function it called; their parameters are those steps' in the record.

step.description: The step's id in the run's plan.

function.description: The dotted name of the function the step called (for example eegprep.clean_asr).

channels.description: The decomposition's channels, the columns of its unmixing, in the recording's order (on the serving copy, store row order).

reference.description: The reference the decomposition's input was in (average for NEMAR's recipes).

unit.description: The unit of the decomposition's input (uV for NEMAR's recipes).

store.description: The store of the serving copy the decomposition read: its path, the channel group read and the group's nemar.store-content.v1 digest. Present exactly when source is serving_copy.

channel_types.description: Every row of the loaded recording, in order, as [label, type], the type as the loader gave it for that row (null for an untyped row): what decided, row by row, which rows were signal channels.

channel_types_sha256.description: The SHA-256, as 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits, of the RFC 8785 canonical JSON of {"channel_types": channel_types}, as UTF-8: the canonicalization of nemar.view-digest.v1 (keys sorted by UTF-16 code units, no whitespace, strings with only the escapes RFC 8785 requires, so a character outside ASCII is written as itself, and no final line feed).

store.description: An input read from the archive names no store.

schemas.title: View Kind nemar.signal-window, Version 1
schemas.description: A window of the recording as the serving copy holds it, opened in the signal viewer, a preset over nemar.lines version 1, applied on top of the envelope to a view declaration whose kind is nemar.signal-window and kind_version 1. The role signal is the recording's store; the window starts at parameters.start_s and lasts parameters.duration_s. The role channels (always) and the role badsegments (when the floor wrote it, parameters.bad_segment_table) are the floor's decisions, which a renderer marks over the window (bad channels and bad segments). Nothing is computed or stored: the view names a window of data the viewer already reads under the dataset's read rule. docs/views/presets.md is normative.

base.description: The window is drawn as lines over time, one per channel.

data.description: The window is read from the serving copy; nothing is stored.

transform.description: The window is drawn as the store holds it.

inputs.description: The roles signal and channels, once each, and badsegments exactly when parameters.bad_segment_table is true.

oneOf.description: The recording's store in the serving copy.

A table of the floor's decisions: the channels (the floor's _channels.tsv, whose status column marks bad channels) or the bad segments (its _badsegments.tsv, onset and duration in seconds), each named by its suffix and written beside the recording (a renderer checks the directory and the shared stem).

allOf.description: The channels are required: the floor always writes _channels.tsv.
At most one badsegments input; whether there is one follows parameters.bad_segment_table (the root's rule).

start_s.description: The window's start, in seconds from the recording's first sample.

bad_segment_table.description: Whether the floor wrote _badsegments.tsv for the recording, as the record names it: true, and the view declares the badsegments input; false (its window step was skipped and ASR repaired nothing), and it declares none and a renderer says nothing is marked.

then.description: A table the record names is declared.

schemas.title: View Transform nemar.sensor-layout, Version 1
schemas.description: Applied on top of the envelope to a view declaration whose transform is nemar.sensor-layout.v1 (docs/views/sensor-layout.md): three-dimensional sensor positions to a layout of theta and radius. The positions are either a stored data role positions, which names its own frame (coordinate_system, or n/a with a montage), so the transform takes no parameters; or the view's one input, the role positions, a TSV file of the run's product with the columns name, x, y and z, whose frame the transform's parameters name. The frame is declared once, never twice.

then.description: Stored positions: the role names the frame, and the view has no inputs.

inputs.description: Stored positions are not also an input.

parameters.description: The positions role names the frame.

else.description: Positions as an input: the parameters name the frame.

inputs.description: The role positions, a TSV file of the run's product.

coordinate_system.description: The Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS) name of the positions' coordinate system, or n/a for template positions that name their montage. Any name passes the schema; the transform refuses one whose orientation it does not know (frame_unknown), and a renderer then places the sensors by name.

montage.description: For template positions: the montage of views/montages they were taken from (nemar.sensor-labels.v1). Every montage file is in a right-anterior-superior frame, in meters, so the coordinate system is then n/a.

schemas.title: View Transform nemar.ic-activity, Version 1
schemas.description: Applied on top of the envelope to a view declaration whose transform is nemar.ic-activity.v1 (docs/views/ic-activity.md), whatever its kind: component activations as one plain multiply, the browser's unmixing matrix times the serving copy's physical values of the decomposition's channels, with no preprocessing. It reads three inputs, each once, and the floor's bad segments (badsegments) exactly when its parameters name them (shaded.files not null): unmixing (a TSV file of the run's product: one column per channel, headed by its label, and one row per component), signal (the recording's store in the serving copy) and components (a TSV file whose column component names the rows of unmixing). The parameters are the record's browser_transform block: the matrix and its columns, how the columns find their store rows (match: store_row, by the rows the decomposition read, or label, by channel label), the unit the matrix takes, a caption, and the spans a view shades.

parameters.description: The view parameters the transform's computation reads, whatever the view's kind: the display filter, the window cap and what the decomposition was given (its store is checked against the signal's).

inputs.description: The roles unmixing, signal and components, each once, and badsegments exactly when shaded.files is not null.

then.description: The matrix and the components table are TSV files of the run's product.
The floor's bad segments are its _badsegments.tsv, a TSV file of the run's product.
The signal is a store of the serving copy.

allOf.description: At most one badsegments input, declared exactly when shaded.files is not null (the root's rule).

parameters.description: The record's browser_transform block (extensions.nemar.ica.browser_transform), as nemar-process writes it: the browser's matrix, what it applies to, how its columns find their store rows, the unit it takes, the caption a view shows, and the spans the view shades.

matrix.description: The matrix's location in the run's product: the location of the input unmixing.

applies_to.description: What the matrix is multiplied by, in words.

note.description: What the activations are, in words (no preprocessing; they approximate the decomposition's input).

match.description: store_row: column j of the matrix is store row rows[j], whose label must be the column's (a decomposition of the serving copy, which read those rows); label: each column is the one store row whose label is the column's (a decomposition of the archive, which read no store).

rows.description: With match store_row, the 0-based store row of each column of the matrix, in column order; null with match label.

columns.description: The matrix's columns, its header names: the decomposition's channels, in column order.

unit.description: The unit the matrix takes: the store's own unit for a decomposition of the serving copy (the factor to microvolts is folded into the matrix), microvolts for one of the archive. Microvolts may be spelled uV, with the micro sign U+00B5 or with the Greek small letter mu U+03BC.

caption.description: A caption a view shows with the activations, or null: for a decomposition of the archive, that they were not checked against the decomposition's input.

shaded.description: The spans ASR repaired in the decomposition's input (flagged in the floor's tables, never removed), which a view shades over the whole recording: the rows whose label is label, in the floor's tables files.

label.description: The label of the shaded rows (burst).

files.description: The table that holds those rows, the floor's _badsegments.tsv, alone, and the location of the badsegments input; or null when the floor wrote no table: its window step was skipped and ASR repaired nothing. _samplemask.tsv is never named: its sample indices are the grid the floor read, not the serving copy the view draws (nemarOrg/nemar-process#81).

rows.description: Columns matched by label name no rows.

caption.description: Columns matched by label were not checked against the decomposition's input, and the view says so: the caption is a string (for nemar-ica, not checked against the decomposition input).

then.description: A decomposition of the archive read no store, so its columns can only be matched by label.
A decomposition of the serving copy read the store's own rows, so its columns are matched by row: never by label, which could find a row the decomposition did not read.

The record names the floor's bad-segment table (shaded.files), so the view declares the badsegments input: a table never read is never drawn silently. The rule is the transform's, so it holds whatever the view's kind: a kind that reuses the transform cannot drop the table (probe p14).
With shaded.files null the floor wrote no table, so the view declares none and a renderer says nothing is shaded.

schemas.title: Checkpoint Counts
schemas.description: Counts of recordings at one processing checkpoint. While a run reports live, passed + failed + skipped <= total; once reconciled, passed + failed + skipped = total. Every checkpoint of one run has the same total (a recording that failed or was skipped earlier counts as skipped later). The writer enforces these invariants; the schema cannot. nemar-cli's live progress object reuses this shape.

failed.description: Recordings that failed at this checkpoint.

skipped.description: Recordings skipped at this checkpoint, including those that failed or were skipped at an earlier one.

schemas.title: Processing Extension
schemas.description: Checkpoint outcomes of NEMAR recipe runs, written by the NEMAR backend. `level` selects the shape: `record` (per recipe, each checkpoint's outcome for one recording) or `dataset` (per recipe, the declared checkpoints and the reconciled counts). Not schema-enforced, enforced by the writer: after a recording's first non-passed checkpoint every later declared checkpoint is `skipped` with the same `code` and `step`; `declared_checkpoints` is the recipe version's registry list in order followed by `stored`, which the backend sets; the keys of `counts` equal `declared_checkpoints`; every checkpoint's counts sum to the same total.

level.description: Which document this entry belongs to: record (one recording) or dataset (the whole dataset).

recipes.description: Checkpoint outcomes per recipe, keyed by recipe id.
Declared checkpoints and reconciled counts per recipe, keyed by recipe id.

recordRecipeOutcome.description: One recording's checkpoint outcomes from one recipe run.

recipe_version.description: Version of the recipe that ran.

checkpoints.description: Outcome per checkpoint, keyed by checkpoint name.

checkpointOutcome.description: A recording's outcome at one checkpoint. A passed checkpoint has no code or step; a failed or skipped one carries its code.

status.description: Whether the recording passed, failed or was skipped at this checkpoint.

code.description: Failure or skip code (the recording's first code, carried to later skipped checkpoints); null when passed.

step.description: The recipe step that failed; null when passed or unknown.

datasetRecipeCounts.description: A dataset's checkpoint counts from one recipe run, reconciled from the run's recordings table.

recipe_version.description: Version of the recipe that ran.

declared_checkpoints.description: The recipe version's checkpoints in order, followed by stored.

counts.description: Reconciled counts per checkpoint, keyed by checkpoint name.

schemas.title: Raw Detail Extension
schemas.description: Detailed per-channel arrays and raw BIDS sidecar content. This extension holds the verbose data that was previously in the core MongoDB documents (channel_names, channel_types, channel_tsv, eeg_json). Separated from core to allow lean queries that skip large arrays.

channel_types.description: Ordered list of channel types (parallel to channel_names).

channel_tsv.description: Parsed content of the BIDS channels.tsv file.

eeg_json.description: Parsed content of the BIDS EEG sidecar JSON (*_eeg.json). Contains task description, equipment info, filter settings, etc.

participant_tsv.description: Parsed row from the BIDS participants.tsv for this subject.

bids_dependencies.description: List of BIDS sidecar file paths that this record depends on.

electrode_tsv.description: Parsed content of the BIDS electrodes.tsv file (electrode names, coordinates).

events_tsv.description: Parsed content of the BIDS events.tsv file (onset, duration, trial_type columns).

schemas.title: DataCite Extension
schemas.description: DataCite-specific metadata for DOI registration (kernel 4.6). Fields here are specific to the DataCite registration format and are not universally needed. Universal scholarly metadata (keywords, related_identifiers, contributors, dates, rights, language) has moved to the core dataset schema as of v0.3.0.

publisher.description: Name of the entity that holds/publishes the data (e.g., 'NEMAR', 'OpenNeuro').

publisher_identifier.description: Persistent identifier for the publisher (e.g., ROR ID for the institution).

publication_year.description: Year when the dataset was first published or made available.

resource_type.description: Free-text description of the resource type (e.g., 'EEG Dataset', 'EMG Dataset').

resource_type_general.description: DataCite controlled vocabulary for general resource type.

geo_locations.description: Geographic locations where the data was collected or about which the data is focused. Coordinates use WGS 84.

place.description: Free-text description of the location (e.g., 'Fudan University, Shanghai, China').

alternate_identifiers.description: Other identifiers for this dataset besides the DOI (e.g., platform-specific IDs like 'nm000108' for NEMAR, 'ds005516' for OpenNeuro).

identifier_type.description: Type or source of the alternate identifier (e.g., 'NEMAR', 'OpenNeuro', 'PhysioNet').

related_items.description: Full bibliographic references for related items (DataCite property 20). Use when you need to cite a resource with complete bibliographic detail (title, authors, journal, pages) rather than just an identifier link.

relation_type.description: Relationship of the related item to this dataset.

publication_year.description: Publication year of the related item.

schemas.title: Data Categories Extension
schemas.description: Study classification metadata for filtering and discovery. Captures the experimental paradigm, clinical context, and cognitive domains of the dataset.

is_clinical.description: Whether the dataset involves clinical populations.

schemas.title: Record Metadata
schemas.description: Per-data-file metadata for an individual recording within a neuroimaging dataset. A data file is a primary recording (e.g., .set, .edf, .vhdr) along with its BIDS sidecar context. Each record has its own modality (required) and can override dataset-level signal properties via signal_properties.

schema_version.description: Envelope field: schema version (present when validated through root schema).

doc_type.description: Envelope field: document type (present when validated through root schema).

dataset.description: Parent dataset identifier (foreign key to dataset.dataset_id).

data_name.description: Human-readable name for this data file (e.g., 'ds002718_sub-004_task-FaceRecognition_eeg.set').

bids_relpath.description: BIDS-compliant relative path within the dataset (e.g., 'sub-004/eeg/sub-004_task-FaceRecognition_eeg.set').

modality.description: Recording modality for this file (e.g., 'EEG', 'MEG', 'MRI', 'iEEG', 'EMG'). Required per record; not inherited from dataset.

file_extension.description: File extension including the leading dot (e.g., '.set', '.edf', '.vhdr', '.fif').

schemas.title: BIDS Entities
schemas.description: Standard Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS) entities parsed from the file path.

schemas.title: Signal Summary
schemas.description: Summary of the recording signal properties. Keeps only aggregate info in core; per-channel details go in extensions. Signal properties that follow BIDS inheritance (sampling_frequency, reference, power_line_frequency) are in inheritable.schema.json instead.

ntimes.description: Number of time points (samples) in the recording.

schemas.title: Record Provenance
schemas.description: Record-level timestamps tracking when a record was digested, created, and last modified.

digested_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when this record was ingested/digested into the system.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when this record was first created.

modified_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of last modification to this record.
